title: liblevenshtein Lua
summary: Fuzzy dictionary search, spelling correction, exact edit distances, bounded query caching, and phonetic matching through Lua 5.4 userdata.

examples.title: Dictionary search and a bounded result cache
examples.description: Construct a libdictenstein dictionary, stream distance-ordered fuzzy matches, preserve valueless membership, and reuse a bounded cache.

entries.name: transducer
entries.description: Retain a libdictenstein dictionary resource. Algorithm defaults to standard; creation does not walk all terms.

entries.name: query_cache
entries.description: Create a bounded result cache (defaults: 1024 entries, 64 MiB weight). Limits must be nonnegative.

entries.name: phonetic_pattern
entries.description: Compile a regular-expression phonetic pattern once for repeated matching and dictionary queries.

entries.name: llre_pattern
entries.description: Compile a named LLRE phonetic pattern.

entries.name: phonetic_rules
entries.description: Parse user rules or select english-orthography or english-phonetic built-ins.

entries.name: distance
entries.description: Compute ordinary Levenshtein distance over Unicode scalar values.

entries.name: distance_threshold
entries.description: Compute Levenshtein distance up to nonnegative maximum.
entries.returns: Distance if within bound; -2 when exceeded on this Lua integer ABI.

entries.name: damerau_distance
entries.description: Compute optimal-string-alignment distance with adjacent swaps; unlike unrestricted Damerau, it is not a metric.

entries.name: damerau_distance_threshold
entries.description: Compute optimal-string-alignment distance up to nonnegative maximum.
entries.returns: Distance if within bound; -2 when exceeded on this Lua integer ABI.

entries.name: true_damerau_distance
entries.description: Compute unrestricted Damerau-Levenshtein distance with history-composable transpositions.

entries.name: true_damerau_distance_threshold
entries.description: Compute unrestricted Damerau-Levenshtein distance up to nonnegative maximum.
entries.returns: Distance if within bound; -2 when exceeded on this Lua integer ABI.

entries.name: query
entries.description: Capture a query-start dictionary revision and search a Unicode-scalar dictionary. Order defaults to traversal.
entries.returns: Cursor of owned Lua match tables.

entries.name: query_bytes
entries.description: Search a byte-domain dictionary; Lua strings may contain NUL and arbitrary octets.
entries.returns: Cursor of owned Lua match tables.

entries.name: query_u64
entries.description: Search a u64-domain dictionary. Pass nonnegative Lua integers through math.maxinteger or exact decimal strings through UINT64_MAX; out-of-range and malformed values are rejected.
entries.returns: Cursor of owned Lua match tables.

entries.name: query_pattern
entries.description: Search the captured dictionary through a compiled phonetic pattern; maximum is an unsigned 8-bit distance.
entries.returns: Cursor of owned Lua match tables.

entries.name: domain
entries.description: Inspect the retained dictionary unit domain.

entries.name: close
entries.description: Release the retained provider; repeated calls are harmless.

entries.name: next
entries.description: Advance the one-shot cursor; refill a bounded native batch as needed. Terms are copied to Lua strings or token tables.
entries.returns: Match {term, distance[, id]} or nil at end.

entries.name: next_batch
entries.description: Copy at most maximum matches into a Lua array; maximum defaults to the native batch size and must be positive.
entries.returns: Array of match tables, or nil at end.

entries.name: reduce_batches
entries.description: Consume successive copied Lua batches with a reducer; the callback result becomes the next accumulator.

entries.name: close
entries.description: Release any native batch lease and the cursor; also invoked by Lua 5.4 __close and __gc.

entries.name: query
entries.description: Query Unicode scalars through the bounded, revision-aware cache.

entries.name: query_bytes
entries.description: Query byte units through the bounded cache.

entries.name: query_u64
entries.description: Query u64 tokens through the bounded cache. Use nonnegative Lua integers through math.maxinteger and exact decimal strings for larger u64 values.

entries.name: stats
entries.description: Read requests, hits, misses, admissions, rejections, evictions, resident_entries, and resident_weight.
entries.returns: A Lua table with eight integer fields.

entries.name: clear
entries.description: Evict all resident entries while retaining the cache configuration.

entries.name: reset_stats
entries.description: Reset counters without evicting resident entries.

entries.name: close
entries.description: Release the native cache; repeated calls are harmless.

entries.name: matches
entries.description: Test a UTF-8 string against the compiled phonetic pattern.

entries.name: size
entries.description: Inspect the compiled automaton's state and transition counts.

entries.name: close
entries.description: Release compiled pattern storage; repeated calls are harmless.

entries.name: apply
entries.description: Apply the selected phonetic rewrite rules; the returned Lua string owns its bytes.

entries.name: len
entries.description: Count rules in the compiled set.

entries.name: close
entries.description: Release the rule set; repeated calls are harmless.

constants.name: merge_and_split
constants.description: algorithm.merge_and_split: symmetric merge and split edits.

constants.name: domain_mismatch
constants.description: status.domain_mismatch: query and dictionary unit domains disagree.

protocols.name: for match in cursor do
protocols.description: The cursor is callable as a Lua generic-for iterator. Explicitly close after early break, or declare it <close>.

protocols.name: local resource <close> = ...
protocols.description: All owned userdata participate in Lua 5.4 lexical cleanup; __gc is only a fallback.

protocols.name: match.term / match.distance / match.id
protocols.description: Each match is an owned Lua table; id is absent if the dictionary term is valueless. U64 terms and IDs use Lua integers in range and exact decimal strings above math.maxinteger.
